source: May et al. (2022), AJ 163, 256, 'A New Analysis of Eight Spitzer Phase Curves and Hot Jupiter Population Trends: Qatar-1b, Qatar-2b, WASP-52b, WASP-34b, and WASP-140b' (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ac6261; arXiv:2203.15059). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of Qatar-1b, 2-3 May 2018, label qa001bo21. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of fit results (table:Results), column qa001bo21. The best fit uses the symmetric phase function (table:bestfits), a first-order sinusoid, so the printed amplitude, (max - min)/2, and hotspot offset, positive eastward, are the whole phase variation.

eclipseDepth.cell: 2922 +/- 163 ppm, F_p/F_S at mid-eclipse ("Day"); the fitted eclipse depth row prints 2914 +/- 162 ppm

model.equation: A symmetric (single cosine) phase function, printed as its amplitude (max - min)/2 and its hotspot offset.

notStated: The table comment gives "Day" and "Night" as phases 0.0/1.0 and 0.5 in that order; the Day flux equals the curve at mid-eclipse (phase 0.5) for every column, and is read so here.
